patch_description: Current approach splits partitions across pre-enumerated k paths, but never lets a later destination (or partition) "hitch a ride" on a trunk already paid for. Since all partitions originate at the same src, once a set of edges has been used, sending additional partitions/destinations over those edges adds (near) zero incremental cost. So: route each partition greedily with Dijkstra on a working copy of the graph whose edge costs are discounted (to ~0) for edges already used in the current pass. Then add an outer refinement loop: re-run the whole routing pass with used_edges warm-started from the previous pass, keeping the pass with the lowest true (undiscounted) total cost. This encourages shared trunks across destinations and partitions, reduces redundant transfers, and converges in 2-3 passes at trivial compute cost.
